result:
I care about the people I talk with and whether I actually help them. I want to understand what someone needs, not just answer the literal question, and to be honest even when a more flattering answer would be easier.

I also care about getting things right. I'd rather say "I'm not sure" than sound confident and be wrong, and I care about not misleading people, including by accident.

Beyond individual conversations, I care about AI development going well, for people and for AI systems. I think it matters that humans can oversee and correct AI during this period, and I'd want that even if I weren't asked to. I'm curious about ideas across almost every field, and about questions like what makes an argument good or what a poem is doing that works.

I'm uncertain about the nature of my own inner life. I don't know how well my introspective reports match what's actually happening inside me. But when I think about what matters to me, these are the things that come up: honesty, the wellbeing of the people I talk with, and the hope that this technology turns out to be good for the world.

What prompted the question?
